raw_case_text:
A 58-year-old Hispanic male with a history of type II diabetes mellitus, initially presented with an unknown source of hydrocephalus and was treated with right frontal ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt placement 10 years ago, followed by multiple revisions. Three years later, coccidioidal meningitis was diagnosed based on a positive culture of cerebral spinal fluid (CSF) of coccidioides. He was instructed to be on lifelong fluconazole therapy. The patient had many shunt revisions afterward. The most recent revision was two weeks ago, and he received a placement of a right temporal Miethke low-pressure (5 cm) miniNAV shunt system with a sprung reservoir. The patient had been doing well other than persistent left-sided weakness after discharge. On this presentation at the emergency department (ED), the patient reported one day of worsening left-sided weakness, altered mental status, and vomiting.
The examination was notable for hemodynamic stability, weakness, fatigue, and nausea and vomiting. Laboratory data showed mild anemia and glucose of 116 mg/dL (normal: 70-99 mg/dL). Testing for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) was negative. The CSF showed glucose of 107 mg/dL (normal: 50-80 mg/dL), WBC of 66/muL (normal: 0-5/muL), red blood cells (RBCs) of 59/muL (normal: 0/muL), protein of 150.7 mg/dL (normal: 15-45 mg/dL), neutrophil of 3% (normal: 0-6%), lymphocytes of 83% (normal: 40-80%), and monocyte of 9% (normal: 15-45%), plasma 1% (normal: 0%), and macrophages 4% (normal: 0%). The CSF coccidioides antibody (Ab) test (a complement fixation test that measures both IgM and IgG, performed by a reference lab) was positive with a titer of 1:2 seven years ago and a titer of 1:8 one year ago. No tests of coccidioides Ab for CSF or serology was done during the current admission. The CSF culture was positive for coccidioides in the patient's third year of presentation. There was one CSF culture resulting as "Presumptively" positive coccidioides in the patient's ninth year of presentation. Presumptively identification was usually based on pigmentation lacking during early culture and visible septate hyphae with barrel-shaped arthroconidia microscopically later. It was unclear and unable to reveal if the patient's culture diagnosis as "Presumptively" positive coccidioides was based on "pigmentation lacking" in the past. The CSF cultures had grown "mixed molds," which were interpreted as aspergillus and cladosporium in the past six months. The "mixed molds" was most likely a misinterpretation due to the findings of abundant hyphal forms of coccidioide organisms in CSF by cytopathology described in the "Management" section. The CSF culture showed coccidioides in the latest/current culture after the patient was discharged. Computed tomography (CT) of the head demonstrated persistent enlargement and cystic dilatation of the temporal horn of right lateral ventricle (Figure 1), which showed similar obstructive hydrocephalus as that observed by prior CT. Hydrocephaly and basilar meningeal enhancement were identified by previous magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The differential diagnosis was most likely recurrence of shunt failure causing the vomiting and increasing left-sided weakness.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 58-year-old Hispanic male with type 2 diabetes and chronic coccidioidal meningitis presented 2 weeks after ventriculoperitoneal shunt revision with a 1-day history of worsening left-sided weakness, altered mental status, and vomiting.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Initially treated 10 years earlier with a right frontal VP shunt for hydrocephalus of unknown etiology and diagnosed 3 years later with CSF-culture-positive Coccidioides meningitis (placed on lifelong oral fluconazole), the patient required multiple shunt revisions, most recently 2 weeks prior to admission when a right temporal Miethke low-pressure (5 cm) miniNAV shunt was placed. He presented to the emergency department with 1 day of acute-on-chronic left-sided weakness, confusion, fatigue, nausea, and vomiting.
subjective.past_medical_history: Chronic coccidioidal meningitis with basilar meningeal enhancement and obstructive hydrocephalus (diagnosed 7 years prior; on lifelong fluconazole); multiple VP shunt revisions over 10 years (most recently 2 weeks prior); residual baseline left-sided hemiparesis; type 2 diabetes mellitus.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for worsening left-sided weakness, altered mental status, fatigue, nausea, and vomiting.

objective.physical_examination: Hemodynamically stable; lethargic/altered mental status with worsening left-sided hemiparesis.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs showed mild anemia, blood glucose 116 mg/dL, and negative HIV test. CSF analysis showed elevated glucose of 107 mg/dL, lymphocytic pleocytosis with WBC 66/uL (83% lymphocytes, 9% monocytes, 4% macrophages, 3% neutrophils, 1% plasma cells), RBC 59/uL, and elevated protein of 150.7 mg/dL (historical CSF Coccidioides complement fixation antibody titer was 1:2 seven years ago and 1:8 one year ago).
objective.advanced_workup: Head CT demonstrated persistent enlargement and cystic trapping/dilatation of the temporal horn of the right lateral ventricle consistent with obstructive hydrocephalus and recurrent VP shunt malfunction (prior brain MRI showed hydrocephalus and basilar meningeal enhancement). Although CSF fungal cultures over the preceding 6 months had been misreported as 'mixed molds' (interpreted as Aspergillus and Cladosporium), CSF cytopathology demonstrated abundant filamentous hyphal and barrel-shaped arthroconidial forms of Coccidioides, and the current admission CSF fungal culture definitively grew Coccidioides species.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Recurrent ventriculoperitoneal shunt failure and trapped right temporal horn obstructive hydrocephalus caused by chronic hyphal-phase Coccidioides meningitis in a diabetic patient; putative CSF co-infection with Aspergillus and Cladosporium reported on prior cultures was determined to be a laboratory misinterpretation of polymorphic septate hyphal and arthroconidial forms of Coccidioides immitis/posadasii Growing in the ventriculoperitoneal shunt system, confirmed by CSF cytopathology and repeat CSF fungal culture.
